name: stlink-autodebug
description: Sets up any STM32CubeMX project to build, flash and debug on a real board (native OpenOCD + GDB), offers to do so when an ST-Link is connected, and builds and runs or debugs it in the ACII simulator.

commands.title: Build & Run in ACII Simulator (debug per checkbox)
Build & Run in ACII Simulator (no debugger)
☐ Debug in ACII Simulator (now: just run)
☑ Debug in ACII Simulator (now: with debugger)
Set Up Project for Board Debugging

stlinkAutodebug.onConnect.description: What to do when an ST-Link is found for an open STM32 project.

stlinkAutodebug.generateFiles.markdownDescription: Files a project needs: `openocd.cfg`, and Build/Flash/Debug entries in `.vscode/tasks.json` and `.vscode/launch.json`. Existing files and entries you edited are never overwritten.
enumDescriptions: When an STM32 project without them is opened, ask before adding anything.
Never offer when a project opens (flashing/debugging still asks if files are missing).

stlinkAutodebug.watchUsb.description: Also react when an ST-Link is plugged in after the project was opened (kernel USB events, no polling). When off, the probe is only checked when the project opens.

stlinkAutodebug.gdbPath.description: GDB with ARM support (a multi-target GDB or arm-none-eabi-gdb). If the default `/usr/bin/gdb` does not exist (Windows), STM32CubeIDE's `arm-none-eabi-gdb` is used, else `arm-none-eabi-gdb`, `gdb-multiarch` or `gdb` from PATH.

stlinkAutodebug.makeCommand.description: make for STM32CubeIDE projects (Debug/makefile). The default runs it in the muvm VM with CubeIDE's toolchain. If `stm32-make` is not installed (Windows), STM32CubeIDE's own `make` is used, with its GNU Tools for STM32 put first in the build task's PATH.

stlinkAutodebug.cubeCommand.description: STM32Cube CLI used to build CubeMX CMake projects (cube cmake --preset Debug).

stlinkAutodebug.simulator.debug.markdownDescription: Debug when running in the ACII simulator: it waits at reset until GDB attaches, then stops at your breakpoints. Off: build and just run it. Also the **Debug** checkbox in the status bar, next to **ACII**.

stlinkAutodebug.simulator.path.markdownDescription: The ACII simulator: its `simulador-acii.sh` (or `panel.py`), or the `ACII_Simulador` folder. Empty: found from its menu entry (`acii-simulador.desktop`) or `~/Downloads/ACII_Simulador`.

stlinkAutodebug.stopAtMain.markdownDescription: Before debugging (board or ACII simulator), add a function breakpoint on `main` to the Breakpoints view if there is none, so the session stops at the start. Untick or remove it there like any breakpoint; turn this off to not have it added again.

stlinkAutodebug.advanceTimeMs.markdownDescription: Milliseconds the **Advance Program Time** button (debug toolbar, while paused) adds to the HAL tick (`uwTick`). Program time stops while paused and a step runs only microseconds of it, so debounces and `HAL_Delay`s never finish when stepping; this skips ahead.

stlinkAutodebug.holdToStep.markdownDescription: In STM32 debug sessions, holding **F10** / **F11** / **Shift+F11** keeps stepping (over / into / out) until the key is released, at `stlinkAutodebug.heldStepRate`. A single press steps once, as usual. Keyboard only: VS Code gives no way to tell a held toolbar button.

stlinkAutodebug.heldStepRate.markdownDescription: Steps per second while a step key is held (`stlinkAutodebug.holdToStep`). Your keyboard's repeat rate is the upper limit, and a step that takes longer slows it down.

stlinkAutodebug.autoAdvanceSteps.markdownDescription: In the ACII simulator, a step (**F10**/**F11**/**Shift+F11**) over code that waits for time, like `while (!tickPass())` or `HAL_Delay`, would never finish: each step runs nanoseconds of program time and the wait needs milliseconds. While a step is still running after 1.5 s, push the HAL tick (`uwTick`) forward by `stlinkAutodebug.advanceTimeMs` every 0.5 s until it ends. Off: step like on a real board (use **Advance Program Time** while paused).
